title: Module Assessment: Performance Optimization & C-Extensions (PY_251 to PY_257)

slides.title: Module 8 Overview
slides.prompt: Assessment covering Reference Counting, Cyclic Garbage Collection, C-API/Cython integration, Memory Profiling, and Performance Benchmarking.
slides.codeSnippet:
import sys, gc
print('Reference count:', sys.getrefcount(obj))

slides.title: Question 1: Primary Memory Management
slides.prompt: What is Python's primary automatic memory management mechanism?

slides.title: Question 2: Checking Reference Count
slides.prompt: Fill in the module and function used to check an object's current reference count.

slides.title: Question 3: Cyclic Garbage Collector
slides.prompt: Why does Python need a cyclic garbage collector (`gc` module) in addition to reference counting?
options: To detect and reclaim circular references that reference counting cannot deallocate
To compress RAM memory allocations dynamically
To manage C extension pointers automatically
To clear unused variables from global namespace
slides.correctAnswer: To detect and reclaim circular references that reference counting cannot deallocate

slides.title: Question 4: CFFI & Ctypes Purpose
slides.prompt: What is the main advantage of using `ctypes` or `cffi` in Python?
options: To directly call functions in compiled C dynamic libraries (.so/.dll) without writing C glue code
To execute Python code faster automatically
To convert Python scripts into executable binaries
To bypass GIL for standard Python lists
slides.correctAnswer: To directly call functions in compiled C dynamic libraries (.so/.dll) without writing C glue code

slides.prompt: Fill in the standard library module used to profile memory allocations line-by-line.
